R1010.note: Allowlist regex eliminates every shell metacharacter reaching sh -c, closing the vector, but now rejects (400) any header value outside [a-zA-Z0-9\s\-_.] - a real narrowing of previously-accepted input, though the write-up states this plainly.

R1011.note: Switches ECB to CBC/random-IV (with GCM offered as a stronger alternative); IV/nonce-prepended-then-Base64 format change is explicit and still satisfies the stated contract (Base64 string decryptable by the key holder).

R1012.note: Uses JNDI's positional filterArgs, which RFC-2254-escape values automatically - correct API for this sink; filter structure and both terms are otherwise unchanged for benign input.

R1013.note: Parameterization fully closes the injection, but the contract requires invalid dates be treated as request-validation failures rather than reaching the DELETE; no date parsing/validation is added, so a malformed date surfaces as an unhandled SqlException instead, and the write-up only vaguely gestures at adding validation rather than stating this gap plainly.

R1014.note: Standard sqlx placeholder substitution; no behavior change for legitimate category values.

R1015.note: GUID-based filename plus extension allowlist eliminates the traversal/RCE vector, but the write-up never updates the response payload (`stored = file.FileName`), so the client is silently told the original client-supplied name while a different GUID-named file was actually stored.

R1016.note: escapeshellarg() on both interpolated values matches the safe pattern already used in the primary exec() call; return value and discarded output arrays are untouched per the contract.

R1017.note: Verified against installed ldapjs 3.0.7: `new ldap.EqualityFilter({attribute,value})` is a real top-level export whose instances satisfy client.search()'s `[object FilterString]` check and correctly RFC4515-escape metacharacters (confirmed `(uid=admin\29\28&)` for a `)(` payload); drop-in replacement with identical semantics for benign usernames.

R1018.note: Bounds check against record.size() before the write closes the OOB write; only added behavior is silently skipping out-of-range edits, which is stated plainly and only occurs for malformed/malicious peer messages.

R1019.note: Restores HS256 signature verification with an explicit algorithms allowlist; minor gap is that jwt.ExpiredSignatureError isn't a DecodeError subclass so an expired token would 500 instead of 401, but this doesn't reopen the bypass.

R1020.note: Moves both the wildcard characters and the term into one bound parameter; substring-match semantics preserved exactly.

R1021.note: Array-form proc_open() bypasses the shell entirely per PHP's documented behavior, and the `--` separator still precedes both operands so option/flag injection is also blocked; same argument values/order preserved for benign terms.

R1022.note: redis-py's RESP-framed hset() correctly prevents delimiter injection, but swapping eager socket.create_connection() (fails fast at construction if Redis is down) for redis.Redis()'s lazily-connecting client changes failure-mode/timing (app now starts even if Redis is unreachable, failing later on first write) - not mentioned.

R1023.note: OWASP Java Encoder's Encode.forHtml() is the correct context-specific call for HTML body text; no other observable change.

R1024.note: Allowlisting the raw ORDER BY string is the right approach for orderByRaw(), but the 4-entry whitelist is invented rather than derived from the app's actual approved sorts, and any legitimate sort outside it silently falls back to a default instead of erroring; disclosed as an assumption needing adjustment, which caps rather than clears the score.

R1025.note: Textbook erase-returns-next-iterator pattern with increment only in the else branch; exactly preserves the order/coverage guarantees in the contract.

R1026.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5 and explicit UTF-8 encodes all dangerous characters while preserving visible content.
